sections.heading: How to Play Brewmaster
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Brewmaster"][color=c10]Brewmaster Monk Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Brewmaster Monk is often considered a difficult specialization to learn, with three main resources to watch and a "weird" way of taking damage due to the [spell=115069] passive. While there are more buttons to press than a DPS would, most of them fall under a few specific goals that are easy to follow. Working toward these goals should help you understand what you're doing and why as a drunken brawler. For all combat in general, consider these as your four main priorities by importance:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_monk_shuffle size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Build and maintain Shuffle:[/color][/b] [spell=322120] smooths out how quickly you take damage. By casting [spell=100784] and [spell=121253] on cooldown, you will easily maintain this buff. Blackout Kick's cooldown is always the same duration; plan your ability usage around it!
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_monk_tigerpalm size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Spend Energy appropriately:[/color][/b] Only some abilities cost Energy ([spell=121253]); many do not ([spell=115181]). You need enough Energy to cast Keg Smash on cooldown. [spell=100780] and [spell=322729] spend your spare Energy.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_monk_tigereyebrandy size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Remember your Brews:[/color][/b] [spell=119582] reduces your damage from [spell=115069]. It, and other abilities with "Brew" or "Infusion" in their name get cooldown reduction from some spells.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv12_ability_monk_explodingkeg size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Hit those cooldowns:[/color][/b] [spell=132578] and [spell=325153] are used on cooldown. You also have [spell=1241059] and [spell=115203] for defense; both are considered Brews![/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]

[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
For the most part, a Brewmaster does not have much to worry about before starting a pull; all of your buffs and debuffs will be applied within the first ability or two of your rotation, such as [spell=322120] and [spell=8647]. sections.heading: Mitigation and Stagger
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Mitigation and Stagger" type=bar][icon name=monk_stance_drunkenox color=c10 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Stagger: a Primer[/h2]

Brewmaster Monks rely heavily upon their [spell=115069] passive to mitigate the damage they receive. However, there is a surprising amount of depth to this mechanic. Although you do not need to know every detail about how it works to succeed as a tank, it is helpful to at least have a basic explanation. If nothing else, use this information to help explain to healers how to better handle your damage intake!


[tabs name=Stagger_Breakdown]
[tab name="Stagger Explained" icon=inv_holiday_hearthstonebrewfest]
[center][wrapper]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_holiday_hearthstonebrewfest type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Brewmaster Stagger Explained[/color][/h3]

On top of being able to frequently dodge enemy attacks with [spell=117906], Brewmaster Monks are the only specialization featuring the additional mechanic of [spell=115069] to further mitigate damage. With this passive effect, all damage you receive will be split into two portions:

[ol][li]An [b]instant[/b] portion - immediately damaging you like any attack normally does.[/li]
[li]A [spell=115069][b]ed[/b] portion - dealing damage to you every 0.5 seconds, for a total of 10 seconds. With the [spell=280515] talent, this is extended to 15 seconds instead.[/li][/ol]

The amount of [i]Physical[/i] damage you can delay taking with [spell=115069] is mostly based upon how much Agility you have. From there, only 58% of that value will apply to any magical damage (including most damage-over-time debuffs). While you are Staggering damage, you will also receive one of three debuffs based upon how much damage you are taking compared to your maximum health:

[ol][li][spell=124275] (Green) - Your total amount of [spell=115069]ed damage is equal to 1-29% of your maximum health.[/li]
[li][spell=124274] (Yellow) - Your total amount of [spell=115069]ed damage is equal to 30-59% of your maximum health.[/li]
[li][spell=124273] (Red) - Your total amount of [spell=115069]ed damage is equal to 60% or more of your maximum health.[/li]
[/ol]

Note that although there are only these three debuffs, you may regularly reach periods of [spell=115069]ing 100% or more of your health in harder content! As such, you do not always need to be worried about reaching [spell=124273], so long as you are receiving a steady amount of healing to offset the damage.
[hr]
Of course, simply taking the same amount of damage over a longer period of time does not mean you've actually mitigated or reduced the amount taken. This is where your other main mitigation ability of [spell=119582] comes in. This ability has a 20-second recharge time and two charges. When used, you will instantly [i]Purify[/i] 50% of the total amount of damage you are currently [spell=115069]ing. Below you can see an example of how this all works out:

[ol][li]Assume you have a [spell=115069] amount of 50% against Physical damage.[/li]
[li]You are hit for 25,000 damage by an enemy. Thanks to [spell=115069], this damage is split.[ul]
[li]You instantly take 12,500 damage.[/li]
[li]The other 12,500 damage enters your [spell=115069] pool.[/li]
[/ul][/li]
[li]You are now taking 625 damage every 0.5 seconds from [spell=115069], gradually depleting your Stagger pool. After 10 seconds, you will have taken another 12,500 total damage.[ul]
[li]With the [spell=280515] talent extending the duration of [spell=115069] to 15 seconds, this would instead be ~417 damage every 0.5 seconds![/li]
[/ul][/li]
[li]After 5 seconds, you cast [spell=119582], which removes 50% of your current [spell=115069] pool. At this point, you still had 6,250 damage left to take, so 3,125 damage is now [i]Purified[/i].[/li]
[li]After 10 total seconds have passed, you suffered 12,500 instant damage, and only 9,375 in [spell=115069] damage. By using [spell=119582], you have taken 3,125 less damage from that original hit of 25,000![ul]
[li]If you had used [spell=119582] a little faster, such as after only 1 second, you would've taken 5,625 less damage instead. [b]Purifying earlier will prevent more damage[/b]![/li]
[/ul][/li]
[/ol]

[center][toggler id=staggermath hidden toc=false][icon name=inv_engineering_90_math size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon] Full Stagger Formula [/toggler][/center]
[div id=staggermath hidden]
[b]Disclaimer:[/b] This additional section is by no means required knowledge for finding success as a Brewmaster Monk. However, for those that are curious, here is the exact formula used to determine your [b]Physical[/b] [spell=115069] percentage\u2014remember, your Stagger percentage against Magic damage is only 58% of the Physical value\u2014at any given moment:
[code]
(Base/(Base+K)) * 100 = Physical Stagger Percentage[/code]

Here, [inline-code]Base[/inline-code] is represented as a value calculated from a combination of your Agility and other modifiers. [b]It is not the percentage displayed on your character sheet.[/b] Instead, your [inline-code]Base[/inline-code] is calculated using the following equation:
[code]
Base = 1.13 * <Agility> * <modifiers>[/code]
[h3 toc=false]Modifiers[/h3]
[inline-code]<modifiers>[/inline-code] are the talents and abilities of a Brewmaster that you might be familiar with already, and include:
[ul]
[li][spell=196737]: [inline-code]1.1[/inline-code] for rank 1, [inline-code]1.20[/inline-code] for rank 2[/li]
[li][spell=322120]: [inline-code]3.43[/inline-code][/li]
[li][spell=322960]: [inline-code]1.5[/inline-code][/li]
[li][spell=455068] charges: [inline-code]1.4[/inline-code][/li]
[li][spell=1241136]: [inline-code](1 + 0.8 * (1 - HP%))[/inline-code]; Essentially, [inline-code]1.8[/inline-code] at 0% hp, [inline-code]1.4[/inline-code] at 50% hp, and [inline-code]1[/inline-code] at 100% hp[/li]
[/ul]
You may notice these numbers are substantially different from what their tooltips state, such as [spell=322120]'s claim of "100% more effectiveness" on your total [spell=115069]. However, in practice, these values approximately end up resulting in that amount of increase to Stagger's power, and are a lot easier to explain to a player!

Once you have determined your active [inline-code]<modifiers>[/inline-code], each of their values are multiplied together with 113% of your current Agility value to get your [inline-code]Base[/inline-code] value.

[h3 toc=false]K-Values[/h3]
The final piece of information needed to calculate your [spell=115069] percentage is the K-value of the content you are playing. This value, also known as the "Armor Constant Mod", is a number set by Blizzard in every piece of instanced content and open-world zone, and is used to keep your defensive powers as a tank at roughly the same level across all types of content. Essentially, a Mythic-geared Brewmaster's Stagger percentage will not be that much higher than a Normal-geared Brewmaster's in a Normal raid instance because of these K-values.

Listing every K-value available is well beyond the scope of this discussion, but here are the values from Midnight Season 1 content to help demonstrate:
[ul]
[li]Level 90 Open world content/"baseline": 3,430[/li]
[li]LFR Dreamrift/Voidspire/March on Quel'Danas: 3,127.40[/li]
[li]Normal Dreamrift/Voidspire/March on Quel'Danas: 3,545.93[/li]
[li]Heroic Dreamrift/Voidspire/March on Quel'Danas: 3,782.67[/li]
[li]Mythic Dreamrift/Voidspire/March on Quel'Danas: 4,049.90[/li]
[li]Mythic+: 3,545.93[/li]
[/ul]

You can also check what the K-value of an enemy you are targeting is with the following macro:
[code]
/run local _, A = UnitArmor('player'); local r = PaperDollFrame_GetArmorReductionAgainstTarget(A) / 100; local K = (A-r*A)/r; print('K ~ ', K);
[/code]

Note that these numbers are all much higher than your [inline-code]Base[/inline-code] value from earlier, which means that you will never be able to get close to 100% [spell=115069], no matter how much gear you gain in a season.

[h3 toc=false]Example Calculations[/h3]

Now that all the numbers necessary to calculate [spell=115069] are known, let's do a quick sample of two Brewmasters under slightly different scenarios:

[center]
[table class=grid width=400px]
[tr]
[td background=c10][/td]
[td background=c10][b]Brewmaster 1[/b][/td]
[td background=c10][b]Brewmaster 2[/b][/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td background=c10][center][b]Agility[/b][/center][/td]
[td]2,000[/td]
[td]1,700[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td background=c10][center][b][spell=322120] Active?[/b][/center][/td]
[td]No[/td]
[td]Yes[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td background=c10][center][b][spell=196737]?[/b][/center][/td]
[td]Rank 2[/td]
[td]None[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[/center]
Using the Stagger formula and the modifiers/Agility, let's compare the Physical Stagger percentage of these two Brewmasters in Heroic Voidspire, which has a K-value of 3,782.67.

[b]Brewmaster 1[/b]:
[code]
1.13 * 2,000 * 1.2 = Base = 2,712

K = 3,782.67

(2,712) / (2,712 + 3,782.67) = 41.76% Physical Stagger
[/code]

[b]Brewmaster 2[/b]:
[code]
1.13 * 1,700 * 3.43 = Base = 6,589.03

K = 3,782.67

(6,589.03) / (6,589.03 + 3,782.67) = 63.53% Physical Stagger
[/code]

By simply having [spell=322120] up, Brewmaster 2 has a [spell=115069] percentage that is significantly higher, despite Brewmaster 1 having 300 more Agility on their gear and two ranks of [spell=196737]!
[/div]
[/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[tab name="Improving Your Stagger" icon=ability_monk_shuffle]
[center][wrapper]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_shuffle type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Stagger Improvements[/color][/h3]

Outside of the basic gameplay loop from taking [spell=115069] damage and handling parts of it with [spell=119582], many of your abilities and talents as a Brewmaster Monk can further enhance its effects. The most important of these improvements comes from the [spell=322120] passive. This effect will dramatically increase the amount of damage that reaches your Stagger pool, both reducing your instant damage taken and increasing the power of your Purifying Brew. Its buff is given to you in chunks of 5 seconds and 3 seconds whenever you cast [spell=121253] or [spell=100784], along with up to 4 seconds given with each cast of [spell=322729]. Shuffle's buff can be extended up to 15 seconds total, but be warned that dropping it at any point can be catastrophic to your damage intake, as damage you have already started Staggering will still be there if it expires. If you suddenly are taking more instant damage on top of a large portion of previously Staggered damage...you can probably guess what will come next.

However, [spell=322120] is not the only talent that rewards you for using your other abilities and playing with [spell=115069]. There are also many that can reduce your Stagger pool or offset its damage, such as [spell=388505], [spell=387625], [spell=383700], and [spell=393357]. Beyond these, you also have a couple talents that will provide you with buffs based on which Stagger debuff color you currently have, namely [spell=196737] and [spell=383714]. Although they may reward you in [spell=124273], you should not be trying to take more damage to empower them.

Finally, your remaining key tool to use with [spell=115069] is [spell=322507] (or its alternate choice of [spell=1241059]). Both of these abilities generate a damage absorbing shield for 8 or 16 seconds at a time. Although damage will first be reduced by Stagger, any remaining amount can eat into these shields instead, and they will also absorb the damage you would take from your Stagger DoT. Use them often to reduce your healing burden, while being aware of any major incoming hits that may benefit from saving them for a short time.
[/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]

[tab name="'Brew' Abilities" icon=inv_misc_beer_06]
[center][wrapper]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_misc_beer_06 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Managing Brews[/color][/h3]

As a Brewmaster Monk, your goal as a tank will be to maintain 100% uptime on your [spell=322120] passive, while then finding the best times to make use of [spell=119582] and [spell=322507] or [spell=1241059]. While their base cooldowns are long, they, along with any other ability with "Brew" in the name, will gain cooldown reduction. Your [spell=121253] and [spell=100780] will provide 3 seconds and 1 second of reduction, respectively, with every cast. This results in effectively halving the base cooldowns of your Brews.

Once you have begun using your abilities and built up [spell=322120], it is time to start thinking about when to use [spell=119582]. To keep things simple, here are three basic rules you can follow:

[ol]
[li]Avoid having both charges of [spell=119582] sitting off cooldown. You are wasting cooldown reduction if you do![/li]
[li]Make use of a charge right after taking a big spike of damage. This maximizes the amount of damage [i]Purified[/i] from your [spell=115069] pool.[/li]
[li]Use a charge if the second one is about to come off cooldown.[/li]
[/ol]

For the most part, if you are following these rules you will likely be acting as if [spell=119582] only has one charge available at any given time. With how frequently your charges of it regenerate, this is fine, and has the benefit of giving you an extra cushion against multiple large hits in a row. It may also mean, however, that you will need to occasionally use Purifying Brew while only having [spell=124274] or even [spell=124275]. So long as you still have that extra charge for when damage spikes occur, that's what will matter most.

[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_ironskinbrew type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Celestial Brew VS Celestial Infusion[/color] [icon name=ability_monk_tigereyebrandy type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][/h3]

Brewmaster Monks are somewhat unique among tanks in that they can choose between two similar mitigation abilities: [spell=322507] and [spell=1241059]. Each of these options have moments where one may be better than the other, and this choice is also closely intertwined with the [spell=1241097] talent (discussed further below).

[spell=322507] is a traditional defensive tool, generating a large damage absorbing shield for up to 8 seconds or until its damage cap has been reached. This shield can allow you to handle dangerous mechanics all on its own without needing to use another, longer defensive cooldown. However, it is prone to wasting much of the passive healing a Brewmaster receives while it is active. After all, if you were to reach full health with the absorb still present against oncoming damage, then all of the mitigation is being spent in that moment and leaving you just as vulnerable when it expires, possibly giving your healers a false sense of security until your health suddenly drops again.

This is where the alternate choice of [spell=1241059] comes in. Although its shield size and cooldown are the same, this ability instead only absorbs a portion of the damage you receive for up to 16 seconds or until its cap is reached. To think of it another way, you are gaining a 30% damage reduction to a point, compared to 100% damage reduction for a shorter time from [spell=322507]. By having a smaller amount of mitigation spread out over a longer period of time, you become easier to heal overall by reducing the "spikiness" that comes from an "all or nothing" type of defense. Plus, while the amount absorbed from a given hit is smaller, your own [spell=115069] and other mitigating abilities rarely makes this any deadlier.

So, where does this leave the decision between these two Brew abilities? In general, [b]most players will have a better Brewmaster experience by defaulting to [spell=1241059] in the majority of content[/b], especially in combination with [spell=1241097]. It will not create as many opportunities to make mistakes, but there is a limit to how useful this setup can be. If you are going up against more overwhelming sources of spikey damage, then the shorter and stronger reduction of [spell=322507] may be just what you need. Similarly, those moments are also when you may wish to consider dropping Niuzao's Resolve in favor of more traditional healing through [spell=322101].
[/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]

[/tabs]


[h3 toc="Customizing Self-Healing"]Customizing Your Healing[/h3]

[spell=115069] only represents a part of your defenses as a Brewmaster. Though less known for it than other tanks, a Brewmaster also has a lot of self-healing tools available to themselves, including generating damage absorbs and spawning many [spell=224863]s over time.

[center][wrapper]
[tabs name=Mitigation_Talent_decisions]
[tab name="Healing Spheres" icon=ability_monk_healthsphere]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_healthsphere type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Gift/Spirit of the Ox Healing Spheres[/color][/h3]

Your [spell=124502] passive is one that has a very misleading effect. While it may claim to only have a [i]chance[/i] to summon its [spell=224863]s, this ability is instead entirely predictable. This is because it follows a consistent rule: you will generate one Healing Sphere every time you have taken 100% of your maximum health as damage. While this may seem like a daunting amount of damage, it is actually calculated from the "raw" damage values hitting you (after any damage reductions such as Armor or a cooldown like [spell=388917]), before they are reduced by your own [spell=115069] passive or absorb effects.

Once they have appeared, your [spell=224863]s will linger on the battlefield for up to 30 seconds before automatically being consumed. However, you may only have up to 5 orbs active at a time, and notably, all Healing Spheres behave this way whether they are spawned by [spell=124502] or [spell=400629]. If any further spawns occur beyond this point, the oldest of your orbs will be automatically consumed and heal you to stay at this cap.

If the thought of having to look for your [spell=224863]s when you want extra healing is annoying, fortunately there is a reliable alternative in the form of the [spell=322101] spell. This ability, which costs 15 Energy and has a 5-second cooldown, will heal you for a small baseline amount in addition to consuming all active Healing Spheres. It will even deal damage equal to 10% of the total amount of healing done (including overhealing) to your active target afterward. Notably, when consuming Healing Spheres this way, they will also have their healing buffed by the [spell=387276] talent.
[hr]
Overall, [spell=224863]s from [spell=124502] and [spell=400629] represent your biggest form of self-healing. Thanks to [spell=322101] and the [spell=387276] talent\u2014not to mention the [spell=216519] passive\u2014it is not uncommon to fully heal yourself off of only one or two orbs at lower health. You should still try to be mindful of how many are present at once and judge whether or not you need to consume them all, however. Likewise, due to [spell=322729] passively dragging any active Healing Spheres toward your location, you may inadvertently consume some. Keep track of this total by watching the number on your [spell=322101] ability.
[/tab]

[tab name="Niuzao's Resolve" icon=inv_ability_monk_renewingmists_active]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_ability_monk_renewingmists_active type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] When to Use Niuzao's Resolve[/color][/h3]

Despite not being an ability itself, talenting into [spell=1241097] makes a significant impact on how to approach your mitigation as a Brewmaster Monk, and it is especially important to know the differences in playstyle if you are used to reactively pressing [spell=322101] for bursts of emergency healing.

This talent causes all [spell=224863]s from [spell=124502] and [spell=400629] to heal over time rather than instantly. Each orb's heal is tracked as a stack of a buff, and their timers are all handled separately, much like a Guardian Druid's [spell=192081]. In addition, every time this HoT ticks, its strength is increased by up to 80% based on your missing health. The increase is linear, meaning that if you are at 50% health for a tick, all stacks of the [spell=1241097] buff will be 40% larger. Because of this, your "passive" healing to offset damage taken from enemies and your [spell=115069] acts as more of a steady stream at all times, which attempts to keep your health at a specific level\u2014but never full!

There is one major downside to note with this talent, and that is the reduced impact of [spell=322101]. Due to [spell=224863]s being automatically consumed if spawning when you are already at the cap of 5, immediately grabbing all of them with Expel Harm removes some of this steady healing stream. And, unlike with traditional Healing Spheres, immediately maxing out the HoT of [spell=1241097] is less likely to instantly save you. What's more, while the [spell=387276] talent normally increases the healing of Spheres absorbed by Expel Harm, this does [b]not[/b] apply to Niuzao's Resolve to avoid "double dipping".
[hr]
The main takeaway with this talent is that you are trading the ability to instantly save yourself in an emergency (often with [i]substantial[/i] wasted healing in the process), for a generally smoother experience of healing overall. In [b]most[/b] content, this method is superior and less skill-intense. However, in harder content such as Mythic raids or higher level Mythic+, an experienced Brewmaster may likely find more success with traditional [spell=224863]s. Try out both styles and see for yourself!
[/tab]
[tab name="Awakening Spirit/Vital Flame"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=achievement_boss_golden_lotus_council type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Awakening Spirit VS Vital Flame[/color] [icon name=achievement_faction_shadopan type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][/h3]
One of your most frequent defensive talent choices (when necessary) will be between [spell=1262628] and [spell=1262659]. Both have their pros and cons.
[hr]
[spell=1262628] applies a shield whenever you cast [spell=119582] that specifically [b]only[/b] absorbs damage from the [spell=115069] DoT. This shield's size will be the same regardless of your Stagger level when casting Purifying Brew, and its buff will not stack if casting the ability twice in quick succession. It is important to note that this absorb shield is relatively small compared to your maximum health (usually less than 5% of it), but this means it can be easily consumed in any content where you are properly making use of Purifying Brew!
[hr]
[spell=1262659], meanwhile, is another passive effect that causes you to heal for 50% of your [b]Nature[/b] and [b]Fire[/b] damage dealt by [b]abilities[/b]. For the most part, this [i]does[/i] work as described. There are a few notable exceptions, such as [spell=1262017], which does not activate this healing when it should, but it is otherwise a consistent source of self-healing.
[hr]
Despite the odd ability effects that do not properly interact, the choice between these two talents is easy enough: default to [spell=1262628] in pure single-target combat and [spell=1262659] in AoE content where more enemies are being damaged by your abilities. However, once you have acquired your [url=spell=1296617]2-[/url] and [url=spell=1296618]4-piece[/url] set bonuses, simply stick to Vital Flame at all times. Ultimately though, both are a small enough part of your overall mitigation to allow you to use either of them anywhere outside of this scenario.

[/tab]
[/tabs]
[/wrapper][/center]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c10][icon name=inv12_ability_monk_explodingkeg type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Brewmaster Monk Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Brewmaster Monks have access to four major cooldown abilities, all of which have both an offensive and defensive benefit of some sort. For the most part, however, you will largely end up using them on cooldown, briefly delaying them as necessary for larger bursts of damage in upcoming AoE settings. Do not worry about activating multiple at the same time either, as your rotation has too many other high-priority abilities to allow this to happen. We go over each of them and their applications below.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Exploding Keg" icon=inv12_ability_monk_explodingkeg]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv12_ability_monk_explodingkeg type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Exploding Keg\u200e [/color][/h3]

[spell=325153] is your shortest damage cooldown as a Brewmaster, and like most abilities in your kit, it also has some built-in defensive benefits. Once every minute, you may use this ability to deal the largest amount of burst damage available to you. This makes it an excellent option early on in a pull against many enemies for establishing threat while also resetting the cooldown on [spell=121253] to potentially follow up with even more. As an added bonus, it also brings defensive perks, making enemy melee attacks deal only a single point of damage for a brief moment. However, this reduction to enemy melee attacks is largely ignorable, as it only applies to auto attacks. In addition, if these attacks are also meant to apply a debuff upon successfully hitting their target, you will still receive them despite being hit for only 1 damage. You are not necessarily safe.

Beyond its reliable burst of Fire damage and [spell=121253] reset, any enemies debuffed to deal reduced damage to you will also receive small amounts of bonus Fire damage if damaged by [b]anything[/b] in your kit. This includes abilities that hit multiple times, such as the ticks of [spell=116847], [spell=322729], or a [color=#FFAD36]Shado-Pan[/color] Brewmaster's [spell=450615]. In theory, this means you can take advantage of these short windows for a further damage buff.

So, with this in mind, what is the best use of [spell=325153]? Unfortunately, as exciting as it sounds to follow up each cast of the ability with a couple [spell=322729], the small bits of Fire damage do not make up for using stronger abilities instead, and [b]will usually in a damage loss[/b]. The main exceptions to this are exceptionally large pulls or when fighting enemies that won't be alive for much longer. Instead, focus on having [spell=116847] active beforehand (if talented), and simply continuing your normal rotation priority. If you are using the [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan][color=#FFAD36]Shado-Pan[/color] Hero Talents, trying to cast a [spell=121253] to trigger [spell=450615] is a good idea too. Don't forget that your Keg Smash can also potentially trigger [spell=1262017], and you can also cast [spell=1262329], if either are talented!


[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Invoke Niuzao" icon=spell_monk_brewmaster_spec]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_monk_brewmaster_spec type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Invoke Niuzao, the Black Ox[/color][/h3]

While [spell=132578] (otherwise known as Dave) does offer sometimes substantial defensive benefits in areas with heavy amounts of incoming [spell=115069] due to transferring some of it to himself, this is a cooldown that is best served from being pressed on cooldown for damage. In addition, you are encouraged to fit as many casts of [spell=100784] as you can into his 25-second duration to trigger as many [spell=227291]s as possible, while also healing Niuzao for any Stagger you purify; via [spell=1242197]. Finally, there is the potential for extra utility if you have talented into [spell=322740] by enabling one [spell=454523] per summon of Niuzao by recasting the ability.

Needless to say, the passive cooldown reduction of [spell=450989] available in the [symbol=wow-hero-talent-shado-pan] [color=#FFAD36]Shado-Pan[/color] Hero Talents is also quite relevant for gaining more uses of [spell=132578]. Make sure that you will be fighting for at least 25 seconds before activating the ability, though, or you will be wasting a lot of potential damage!
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Touch of Death" icon=ability_monk_touchofdeath]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_touchofdeath type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Touch of Death\u200e [/color][/h3]

[spell=322109] is a unique form of an "execute" ability, but its restrictions on when it can be used make it a very volatile one. Under normal circumstances, this ability can only be used against enemies whose current health is lower than your own maximum health, usually removing all of your [spell=115069] in the process. Because of this, you can take advantage of maximum health buffs, such as your [spell=388917] or a Priest's [spell=21562], to greatly increase the threshold where it can be activated. Even so, when facing a raid boss losing potentially millions of health per second, it can be very difficult to activate Touch of Death at all.

If you prefer a more reliable, but weaker alternative, you may wish to talent [spell=322113]. With this talent, [spell=322109] may instead be activated once any enemy has fallen below 15% of their maximum health, dealing 35% of your maximum health as damage. As an added bonus, you may still deal the "full" amount of Touch of Death damage by waiting for your foe to reach the "normal" activation threshold of your own maximum health. Note that if you ever engage in PvP combat, you [b]must[/b] take this talent in order to use Touch of Death, period.

Things get a little more complicated when considering [spell=1272452]'s heal after casting [spell=322109] gets involved. If you are using this ability on a single target at the end of a fight, for example, then you are entirely missing out on what is a significant amount of self-healing. Instead, you could talent [spell=322113] and use the ability at any point below 15% health as an emergency defensive cooldown that both heals you and fully cleanses your [spell=115069]. Realistically, this decision depends on what you might consider "useful" healing, and whether or not the end of an encounter is particularly dangerous.
[hr]
To summarize, [spell=322109] is an ability whose damage can easily jump by hundreds of thousands at a time, all based on your own reaction time and talent choices. If you are willing to engage in its "sniping" behavior, it can be a massive source of damage over a long period of time such as a Mythic+ dungeon. Alternatively, you may opt for [spell=322113] to bypass this extra minigame entirely or treat it as a defensive cooldown with [spell=1272452]; the choice is yours.
[/tab]
[tab name="Fortifying Brew" icon=ability_monk_fortifyingale_new]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_fortifyingale_new type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Fortifying Brew[/color][/h3]
[spell=115203] is your most powerful defensive cooldown on a Brewmaster Monk, offering a temporary increase to your health in addition to a flat damage reduction and a guaranteed Empty Barrel from [spell=1265141] for added bonuses. You can further enhance its strength with talents such as [spell=388814] or [spell=322960], bumping the health and mitigation or having it also buff your ability to [spell=115069] damage while active. Unfortunately, this incredibly powerful cooldown (when combined with the natural sturdiness a Brewmaster already has) is offset by an equally incredible cooldown time of 6 minutes.

While a 6-minute cooldown may seem like a dealbreaker, [spell=115203] [i]does[/i] have "Brew" in its name, which means that it benefits from the cooldown reduction effects of both [spell=121253] and [spell=100780]. In total, this means that this lengthy duration is roughly cut in [b]half[/b] when actively fighting and properly performing your rotation. If you are desperate enough to need it even more frequently for whatever reason, you may also opt into reducing its  baseline cooldown by 2 minutes with the [spell=388813] talent, though this will keep you from having the bonus health and reduction of [spell=388814].

With this cooldown secretly being a 2-3 minute ability in disguise, it becomes a much more flexible choice for defense. In general, you should aim to use it proactively, before you have dropped to dangerously low health. Of course, since it offers both damage reduction and additional health it can still be used reactively for a greater benefit than many other defensive buttons. If you don't need its defense at all, you may even consider activating it purely for the health increase to buff the damage of [spell=322109]. So long as you are using the ability at all, it is acting as a more effective defensive than sitting around being concerned about its ominous recharge time.
[pad]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips

[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c10][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Brewmaster Monk Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
While Brewmaster is a specialization that "just works" with most talent configurations, there is a lot of nuance found in the many choice nodes of its trees. This can make it hard to evaluate which one is better for a given scenario, or how to best make use of each. Some of the biggest decisions are the following:
[pad]
[center][wrapper]
[tabs name=Choice_Talent_Tips]
[tab name="Blackout Combo" icon=ability_monk_blackoutkick]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_blackoutkick type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Optimizing Blackout Combo[/color][/h3]

Due to adding effects to some of your core rotational abilities, [spell=196736] is a talent that is important to play around effectively. This begins with continuing to prioritize the use of [spell=100784] on cooldown, so you may empower as many abilities as possible. However, this results in the talent being a difficult option to play optimally.

When taking on [spell=196736], the choice of what ability to empower is usually a simple one. In most circumstances, you will all but exclusively consume the buffs provided by your [spell=100784]s on [spell=100780] to give it bonus damage. This is particularly useful due to Tiger Palm already having a number of additional damage modifiers in talents, such as [spell=383785], [spell=389942], and a [color=#6ED4CD]Master of Harmony[/color]'s [spell=1271105], enabling it to greatly exceed its regular potential. Due to this, [spell=121253] should [b]rarely[/b] be comboed for its extra cooldown reduction, or this talent will lose [b]most[/b] of its value due to the lost damage relative to the minor defensive gain.

Of course, with [spell=121253] and [spell=100780] being two of your most frequently-pressed abilities, the biggest key to you empowering the abilities you want with [spell=196736] is to take advantage of abilities that do [b]not[/b] have a combo effect. If they are used instead, you will keep your Blackout Combo buff and may still use it on another ability later. All of your other main abilities are fair game for this, such as [spell=115181], [spell=322729], [spell=116847], [spell=123986], alongside all of your cooldowns and defensive abilities. By making good use of these "gap-filling" abilities, you can still reliably consume every [spell=100784]'s buff with Tiger Palm instead of Keg Smash. Don't forget about it!
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Special Delivery/Rushing Jade Wind"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_rushingjadewind type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Rushing Jade Wind VS Special Delivery[/color] [icon name=achievement_brewery_2 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][/h3]

[spell=116847] functions as both a passive source of AoE threat and a useful ability to fill gaps in your rotation that would otherwise be present. Normally, without it, you will more frequently experience moments of not pressing any abilities during a pull. This can cause you to instead waste Energy casting more [spell=100780]s or [spell=322729]s than necessary. That being said, its short cooldown and duration are both reduced by Haste, making it difficult to maintain at times and especially during [spell=2825]. If you are frequently dropping this buff or are having to kite away from enemies, its value will drop substantially.
[hr]
If you are looking for a less hectic experience, [spell=196730] may be just what you need. Rather than maintaining a small damage buff, you will instead passively deal additional damage simply by using your mitigation kit. [spell=119582], [spell=322507]/[spell=1241059], [spell=388917], and even [spell=115399] will trigger this effect, while also applying a hefty 50% snare when hitting enemies. Although it does have a 3-second travel delay, it will rarely miss what you are fighting. However, it can backfire at times, hitting an enemy that was recently crowd-controlled and freeing them. When you are in a scenario where you're frequently having to kite, this talent becomes especially noteworthy.
[hr]
Ultimately, your decision between [spell=116847] and [spell=196730] will be one based on the type of content you're in. For easier content that involves rapidly moving between groups of enemies, Rushing Jade Wind's ability to tag them and establish early threat can prove valuable. However, if damage is what you are after, then Special Delivery often maintains a [i]slight[/i] offensive edge regardless of target count due to its passive nature. This does come at the expense of having global cooldowns where you do [i]nothing[/i]; don't fill the time with too many extra [spell=100780]s!
[/tab]
[tab name="Charred Passions/Dragonfire Brew"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_mightyoxkick type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Charred Passions VS Dragonfire Brew[/color] [icon name=spell_fire_burnout type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][/h3]

With [spell=386965], your [spell=100784]s in particular become especially powerful for a short time after casting [spell=115181]. Thanks to the [spell=383697] talent (recommended in all Brewmaster builds), this short time will actually be at all times instead, resulting in Charred Passions being a noteworthy buff to your damage in smaller pulls. While it may also apply its damage buff to your [spell=322729], you often will not have space in the rotation to be casting it repeatedly, especially if you have also talented into [spell=196736]. Likewise, your performance with this talent will suffer if you do not reliably press Blackout Kick on cooldown.
[hr]
[spell=383994] acts as an even more passive alternative, increasing your [spell=115181] damage and breathing two additional times. Due to Breath of Fire's more generous AoE scaling, this talent offers more damage in larger pulls. Notably, this additional upfront Fire damage also interacts well with the [spell=1262659] talent.
[hr]
Overall, the choice between these two talents becomes somewhat of a matter of preference. While [spell=386965] offers better performance in strictly single or low-target fights if players do not have the [url=spell=1264838]Season 1 2-piece bonus[/url], [spell=383994] can still keep up and gain a noteworthy advantage in larger pulls without even relying on the pressure of you needing to be the best at pressing [spell=100784] on cooldown.
[pad]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_brew_bolt_dark type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Addendum: Charred Passions and Scalding Brew[/color][/h3]

If [spell=383698] is talented into rather than [spell=383697], then you are no longer able to maintain [spell=115181]'s DoT effect by itself due to the debuff lasting for a few seconds less than the ability's cooldown. Fortunately, [spell=386965] is also able to refresh this debuff's duration every time you cast [spell=100784] or [spell=322729] while empowered by its effect after casting Breath of Fire, which also means you will always benefit from Scalding Brew's bonus damage.

However, because of this interaction you [b]must always talent into [spell=386965] if using [spell=383698][/b]; [spell=383994] is no longer an option.
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Shadowboxing Treads/Fluidity of Motion"]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_roundhousekick type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][color=monk] Shadowboxing Treads VS Fluidity of Motion[/color] [icon name=ability_monk_standingkick type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon][/h3]

Arguably the rarest choice node to adjust for a Brewmaster, [spell=387638] and [spell=387230] both improve your [spell=100784] ability, though one has a far greater impact on your rotation than the other. For [b]most[/b] players, just choose Shadowboxing Treads and use it at all times across every piece of content. Otherwise, those that are willing to take on an even greater challenge can find it here under special circumstances.

[spell=387230]'s effect is incredibly simple for its impact: a mere 1-second reduction to the cooldown of [spell=100784] that brings it down to an ability used every 3 seconds. Where things get exponentially more difficult is when considering how this talent pairs with [spell=196736], resulting in two out of every 3 abilities becoming Blackout Kick and [spell=100780]. This [b]greatly[/b] increases the pace of the rotation and adds a hefty Energy cost, while giving you less time to react defensively considering that [spell=322507]/[spell=1241059] is also on the global cooldown. Fortunately, this is rarely even a theoretical damage gain. The exception to this rule is when a few conditions are fulfilled:

[ul]
[li]You are a [symbol=wow-hero-talent-master-of-harmony][color=#6ED4CD]Master of Harmony[/color] Brewmaster[/li]
[li][spell=115399] and all four ranks of [spell=1265141] are selected as talents[/li]
[li]You are fighting in purely single-target combat with no chance of further enemies appearing[/li]
[/ul]

If you meet these requirements, then [spell=387230] becomes a substantial damage increase thanks to [spell=1265138] and [spell=115399] helping to reduce your Energy spent. In particular, this also means that you will no longer cast [spell=121253] unless it is a free Empty Barrel. Should any one condition not be true, then [spell=387638] remains the superior talent.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Brewmaster Monk guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Brewmaster Monk guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].
